channel.title: Hosting on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Hosting on Best of AI

item.title: Libsyn
item.description:
Libsyn, short for Liberated Syndication, has hosted podcasts since the early days of the medium. Creators upload audio, and Libsyn produces the RSS feed that podcast apps use, so a show appears across Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and many other directories. It also offers an embeddable player and a basic website.

Pricing has historically been based on the amount of storage you upload each month, which differs from plans tied to downloads. Statistics show downloads by episode and location, and the platform has monetization options, including dynamic ad insertion and sponsorship marketplaces, plus tools for video podcasts and premium subscriptions.

item.title: Squarespace
item.description:
Squarespace appeals to people who want an attractive site without a developer. You choose a template, change the content with a visual editor, and publish with hosting, security, and a domain included. Its designs are known for clean layouts and good typography, which makes it popular with creatives, small businesses, restaurants, and portfolio sites.

The platform goes beyond static pages. Built-in commerce handles products, subscriptions, and checkout, email campaigns support marketing, and Acuity Scheduling covers appointments. AI features include a site builder that generates a starting design and content from answers to a few questions, text-writing assistance, and tools for improving search visibility. Analytics show traffic and sales.

item.title: WordPress
item.description:
WordPress is the software behind a large share of the web. You install it on a web host or sign up with a hosted service, and manage pages, posts, media, and users from a dashboard. A block editor lets you build layouts visually, and thousands of themes control how a site looks. Plugins extend it for SEO, contact forms, memberships, caching, analytics, and online stores through WooCommerce.

It comes in two forms that are easy to confuse. WordPress.org is the free software you host yourself, which gives full control and requires handling hosting, updates, and security. WordPress.com is a hosted service from Automattic with plans that handle those chores. AI arrives mostly through add-ons: Jetpack and other plugins offer writing help, image generation, and chat assistants, and AI site builders can generate a first draft of a site from a prompt. The core project is also adding building blocks for AI features.

item.title: Zencastr
item.description:
Zencastr was built for remote podcast interviews. Instead of recording a call, it captures each participant’s microphone on their own device and uploads the separate tracks, which produces cleaner audio than the compressed stream you hear during a call. Guests join through a link in their browser, with no account needed.

Beyond recording, it offers tools for finishing a show. Automatic post-production levels audio and removes silence, an editor allows basic cuts, and AI features generate transcripts, summaries, and show notes. Video recording and a hosting option cover more of the workflow, and exports go to editing programs.

item.title: Hocoos
item.description:
Hocoos aims at people who want a website without a design process. The user answers questions about their business and style, and the AI generates pages, text, and images, and sets up features such as contact forms, an online store, or appointment booking. An editor allows changes afterward.

The platform includes hosting, a domain option, and SEO basics, plus marketing helpers such as email tools and social media content. It is positioned for small and local businesses and solo entrepreneurs who need an online presence quickly.

item.title: Transistor
item.description:
Transistor is designed for people who run more than one podcast. A single account can host unlimited shows, which suits agencies, companies, and networks, and plans are based on downloads and team size instead of per-show fees. Episodes distribute to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other apps through an RSS feed Transistor manages.

Other features address professional needs. Private podcasts let companies share internal or members-only audio, embeddable players and a branded website help promote shows, and detailed analytics show downloads and audience. Collaboration features give team members access to specific shows, and integrations connect with Zapier and other tools. AI tools support transcripts and episode copy.

item.title: 10Web
item.description:
10Web combines site generation with hosting. You describe a business or enter the address of an existing website, and the AI builds a WordPress site with layout, text, and images, which you can then edit with a visual builder based on Elementor. The result is a standard WordPress site, so it can use the plugin and theme ecosystem and can be moved elsewhere.

Hosting and optimization are part of the package. Sites run on managed WordPress hosting with a focus on speed, including automatic optimization of images and code to improve page speed scores, and tools for backups and security. AI features generate copy, images, and SEO suggestions, and an assistant can edit pages based on instructions. Agencies can white-label the platform and manage client sites, and there is an API for builders who want to embed it.

item.title: Buzzsprout
item.description:
Buzzsprout focuses on being the easiest way to get a podcast online. You upload an audio file, add show notes, and publish, and it distributes the episode to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other directories through an RSS feed it manages. It provides an embeddable player for your website, detailed download statistics, and tools for promoting episodes on social media.

Additional features help creators improve and grow. Magic Mastering automatically cleans up and balances audio loudness, an AI transcription service creates transcripts, and tools can generate chapters, episode titles, and descriptions. Dynamic content features and a way to import an existing podcast make switching easy. Monetization options include support from listeners and ads in some plans.

item.title: Cleanvoice
item.description: Cleanvoice does one job: it cleans up speech. You upload a podcast episode, interview, or video, and it finds the places where a speaker said “um” or “uh,” paused for too long, made lip smacks or breath sounds, or repeated a word. It removes them and returns a tidier file. Editing these by hand takes a long time, and a one-hour recording can contain hundreds of them, so automating it saves real hours for podcasters and video creators.

item.title: Descript
item.description:
Descript changed podcast editing by turning audio into text. After you record or import an episode, it transcribes it, and you cut, move, and delete sections by editing the words, which is much faster than working on waveforms. Filler words and long pauses can be removed in bulk, and multitrack editing, music, and effects are available for more polished shows.

Recording and polishing tools are built in. Remote recording captures guests in high quality, Studio Sound improves voice clarity and reduces noise, and an Overdub feature can fix mistakes with a synthetic version of your voice. AI assistants draft titles, descriptions, and show notes, suggest chapters, and generate clips and audiograms for social media. Episodes can be published to hosting platforms or exported.

item.title: Durable
item.description:
Durable promises a website with minimal effort. You tell it the kind of business you run and where you are, and it builds a site with pages, copy, images, and a layout in under a minute, which you can then edit with simple controls. It’s aimed at freelancers and local service businesses, such as plumbers, photographers, and consultants, who need an online presence quickly.

Beyond the site, Durable includes small-business tools. A built-in CRM tracks leads and customers, an invoicing feature handles billing, and AI assistants help write blog posts, social content, and marketing copy. It offers hosting and a custom domain, and basic analytics. Everything lives in one account, so owners avoid piecing together several services.

item.title: Framer
item.description:
Framer started as a prototyping tool and became a full website builder. Designers lay out pages on a canvas much like they do in Figma, set up responsive behavior, add animations and interactions, and publish to a fast hosted site with a custom domain. Because it gives designers precise control over visuals and motion, it’s popular for portfolios, landing pages, and marketing sites.

A CMS manages blog posts and other structured content, and features for SEO, localization, and analytics support production sites. AI tools generate a first draft of a site from a description, create wireframes, and write copy, which speeds up the start of a project. Components and code overrides allow customization when needed, and a marketplace of templates and plugins helps.

item.title: Riverside
item.description: Riverside solves a familiar remote-recording problem: video calls compress audio and video, so the recording sounds and looks poor. Riverside records each person’s microphone and camera on their own device and uploads the files in the background. The result is uncompressed audio and up to 4K video, with each participant on a separate track, unaffected by a weak internet connection during the call. Hosts and guests join through a browser link without installing anything.

item.title: Spotify for Podcasters
item.description:
Spotify for Podcasters grew from Anchor, an app that made podcasting free and easy. Creators can record from a phone or computer, upload episodes, and publish to Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and other directories from one place, with no hosting fees. Tools include simple editing, music and sound effects, and a way to bring in guests remotely.

The creator tools have expanded to include video podcasts, which Spotify has promoted heavily, along with analytics on audience size, demographics, and listening behavior. Monetization options include ad insertion, listener subscriptions, and partner programs for eligible shows. The brand has been folded into Spotify for Creators, which covers audio and video content creators on the platform.

item.title: Wix ADI
item.description:
Wix ADI, short for Artificial Design Intelligence, was an early attempt at automatic site building. A user answered questions about their business and style, and ADI generated a layout with text, images, and a structure suited to the industry. It let people with no design skills get a website online in minutes, long before generative AI was common.

ADI sites had limits. They used a simpler editor than the main Wix Editor, which made it hard to customize them or to add advanced features. Wix has since retired the product: ADI sites are no longer supported and existing ones were moved into the standard Wix Editor, so owners can keep editing them there.

item.title: Podcastle
item.description:
Podcastle is a browser-based studio for audio. Users can record remote interviews with separate tracks, edit by working with the transcript, and clean up audio with one-click enhancement that removes noise and levels voices. A text-to-speech and voice cloning feature lets creators fix a mistake by typing.

The platform includes tools for video podcasts, hosting and distribution, and AI features such as summaries and show notes. It aims to give new podcasters an all-in-one workflow without learning a traditional audio editor.

item.title: InstaWebAI
item.description:
InstaWebAI generates a full website from a short brief. A user enters information about the business, and the tool creates pages, copy, images, and a structure designed for search engines, which can be edited and published. The goal is to cut the time from idea to live site to minutes.

It targets owners who lack design or writing skills and want a professional baseline. Typical outputs include home, services, about, and contact pages, along with metadata for search visibility. Publishing options and domain connections vary by plan.
